title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 74
paragraphs: To this deme belonged Sophanes, who showed himself the best of all the Athenians in this battle. Of him there are two different stories told. One says he carried an iron anchor bound by bronze chains to the belt of his corslet, which he would throw down whenever he came up with the enemy, so (they say) that when the enemy came out of their ranks, they could not move him from his place; and when a flight of his opponents took place, his plan was to take up the anchor first and then pursue them. So this story goes. But the other story, disputing the truth of the one above, reports as follows: on his shield, which was always moving about and never remaining still, he bore an anchor as a device — and not an iron one bound to his corslet.
